title: IPBES
article: Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services

definition.text: An independent intergovernmental body, set up by governments in 2012, that links biodiversity science to policy-making.

facts.text: It plays a role similar to the IPCC, but besides assessments it also builds knowledge, capacity and policy support tools.
A 2010 UN General Assembly resolution asked UNEP to convene a meeting to establish it; its members meet in Plenaries every one to two years.
Its 2019 Global Assessment, adopted by representatives of 132 members in Paris, was the largest study to date of biodiversity and ecosystem services.
A 2020 IPBES report said preventing pandemics through conservation is more cost-effective than responding after outbreaks.
IPBES and the IPCC shared the Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity in October 2022.
In January 2026 the United States announced its withdrawal from IPBES.

title: Nature's contributions to people
article: Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services#Nature's contributions to people

definition.text: The IPBES term for all the ways nature benefits people, adopted in place of 'nature's benefits to people'.

facts.text: The 5th IPBES Plenary in 2017 decided to use the concept in current and future assessments.
It was introduced to bring diverse worldviews, including indigenous and local knowledge, into biodiversity assessments.
Some scientists objected that the term was confusing and not significantly different from ecosystem services.

contested_note: Scientists disagree whether the term adds anything beyond the ecosystem services concept.

title: Biodiversity and climate change nexus
article: Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services#Cooperation with IPCC

definition.text: The idea, set out in a joint IPBES–IPCC report, that climate change and biodiversity loss are linked and must be tackled together.

facts.text: In June 2021 IPBES and the IPCC released a co-sponsored workshop report on biodiversity and climate change.
Efforts to address one problem can worsen the other if their links are overlooked.

title: IPBES Transformative Change Assessment
article: Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services#Transformative Change Assessment

definition.text: An IPBES report, approved on 18 December 2024, on the underlying causes of biodiversity loss and how to bring about transformative change.

facts.text: It builds on the 2019 Global Assessment, which found that only transformative change can achieve global development goals.
The 2019 assessment also warned that society should not focus solely on economic growth given the loss of biodiversity.

title: IPBES Nexus Assessment
article: Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services#Nexus Assessment

definition.text: An IPBES report, approved on 17 December 2024, on how biodiversity, water, food and health are connected.

facts.text: It looks for ways to maximise benefits across five nexus elements: biodiversity, water, food, health and climate change.

title: Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework

definition.text: The global plan for nature adopted at the 2022 UN Biodiversity Conference (COP15) under the Biodiversity Convention.

facts.text: It was adopted on 19 December 2022 and promoted as a 'Paris Agreement for Nature'; it is the most significant CBD agreement to date.
It contains four global goals for 2050 and 23 targets for 2030, and succeeds the Strategic Plan 2011–2020 with its Aichi targets.
Goal A aims to cut the extinction rate and risk of all species tenfold by 2050 and halt human-induced extinction of threatened species.
Target 3, the '30 by 30' target, asks governments to protect 30% of Earth's land and water area by 2030.
Countries are also to stop subsidising activities that destroy wilderness, such as mining and industrial fishing.
Target 13 commits parties to share fairly the benefits from genetic resources and digital sequence information.
It is not legally binding, and its targets are criticised as vague, lacking measurable indicators; by COP16 only 44 of 196 parties had new biodiversity plans.
It is named after Kunming, the original host city, and Montreal, which hosted COP15 after Kunming withdrew because of China's COVID policy.

contested_note: Critics, including the IPBES chair, warn it may yield business as usual because its targets are vague and non-binding.
distinct_from: GBF implications for business and finance

title: GBF implications for business and finance

definition.text: Expected effects of the global biodiversity framework on companies, banks and central banks, according to the UNEP Finance Initiative.

facts.text: Companies are expected to face mandatory disclosure of their impacts on biodiversity.
Banks are expected to shift money into nature-restoring projects, and central banks to treat nature-loss risk as part of their mandates.
Nature-positive, the goal of halting and reversing nature loss by 2030, has helped mainstream the framework in business and governance.
In May 2024 UNEP and China launched the Kunming Biodiversity Fund, with China committing $230 million USD.

definition.text: Sites outside formal protected areas that are governed and managed in ways that conserve biodiversity in place over the long term.

facts.text: Unlike protected areas, OECMs need not be dedicated to conservation, but must deliver effective long-term conservation of biodiversity.
The term first appeared in Aichi Target 11 in 2010, which sought to conserve 17% of land and inland waters and 10% of coastal and marine areas by 2020.
The CBD formalised the definition in 2018 through Decision 14/8 at COP 14, building on Canadian guidelines and IUCN advice.
OECMs count towards Target 3 of the Global Biodiversity Framework.
As of June 2026, 7,488 OECM sites cover 1.31% of Earth's surface, about 1.1% on land and 0.21% at sea.
They allow small-scale uses such as fisheries and low-impact agroforestry and aim to be more equitable than protected areas, which have caused displacement.
Locally managed marine areas are one form of OECM.
